text:
Leaving in the middle of the process means you will NOT be able to return until the process moves through its initial stages. The moment your partner visa file is opened, you cannot re-enter after leaving without the explicit permission of your case worker. Even if you applied according to the regulations and with all documents, which it appears you did not, it isn't guaranteed that MH will issue that reentry permit. In many branches, they won't give it to people who applied from the inside unless there is a very good reason to do so.
So unfortunately, you are left with two options: You can choose to travel, but that will likely mean you will have to stay abroad and wait for a formal invitation by MH, which is usually only issued after the document submission has been concluded both online and offline (during the first meeting attended by your spouse). Or you stay and wait until you receive the visa. You will not receive an A5 btw. For the first 6 months, a married spouse will be given a B1 visa, which is a tourist visa with work permit. Only after those 6 months have passed will you receive temporary residency (A5). This is important because you will need to take care of your private medical insurance during that initial phase. 
One more thing: Are you in contact with your branch of MH? Because usually, when you submit an application with missing documents and your case lands on the desk of a worker who notices, you are given 45 days to submit the missing documents - or you risk a rejection of your application. Those 45 days are not set in stone and when you push for it, they often give you another extension, but that obviously only works when you are proactively managing your case. Also: Afaik, no branch will give you an interview appointment if they established that your online submission is incomplete. 
I totally understand that in life, things are rarely perfect and partners want to avoid separation, but this strikes me as a perfect example for the problems that can arise from an application that is submitted in a rush because the partner is here on a tourist visa and doesn't want to leave.
